hook: The world's factories and warehouses cannot find enough people to fill the jobs it runs on.
Putting robots to work still takes costly engineering, so robots have to learn on their own.
Meet the founder who moved around his whole life and found his one constant in how things work.
He wanted to be an inventor and make his mark, so he studied physics, computer science and engineering.
He followed the inventor path through computer science, physics and engineering, and it led him here.
Starting his own company was always the plan, and Google was just a temporary gig to pay off loans.
Google was a temporary gig, until ChatGPT made him start building software that programs robots.
When ChatGPT arrived, he saw AI could accelerate robotics, and he knew it was time to start.
Robots like the ones in the movies are possible, but robotics today is painful.
Robotics is painful to do today, and we keep seeing demos but never robots in our homes.
We keep seeing robot demos, so why do robots still repeat the same motion over and over?
Robots belong in factories, but the missing piece is an interface that ends monotonous human work.
The real need comes from manufacturers, logistics companies and pharma, and they taught him how to build a company.
Building a company taught him how to sell, how to trust what he is making, and what to ignore.
He knows what to focus on and what not to, and he gets to do it in New York.
Founder stress is real, so he keeps his mind sharp by exercising and working out.
As a founder, no two days look alike: the office, home, a warehouse, then investors in Hudson Yards.
Some days he is in the office, some at home, some in a warehouse, some pitching in a skyscraper.
80% of the world's GDP is tied to physical labor, and robots are still stuck on repeat.
For the first time, anyone can teach a robot new skills just by talking to it.
He started this company because there is a better way to do robotics, and it can change the world.
Software that programs robots could finally give us robots like the ones in the movies.
It doesn't feel like work when you love the problem and it can change the world.
